name: Strapi
tagline: A headless CMS with a Node.js server, an admin interface, and a plugin ecosystem.
hook: A Yarn and Nx guide to content access, dependency injection, shared types, edition boundaries, tests, skills, and migrations.
summary: Strapi's root guide maps its Yarn and Nx monorepo and sets boundaries for content access, dependency injection, shared types, and edition-specific code. Test areas use separate commands, while committed skills live in one directory and link into each tool.

techniques.title: Name the exception to a sandbox-only rule
techniques.body: Example apps normally reproduce fixes rather than receive production changes. The guide names examples/complex as the exception because CI uses it as a migration fixture.

techniques.title: Keep skill sources independent of tool-specific paths
techniques.body: Committed skills live in .ai/skills. A sync command creates or prunes local links for Agents, Claude, and Cursor, with Windows junctions supported and a read-only status command for diagnosing missing or conflicting links.
techniques.quote: **`.ai/skills/`** is the canonical source for committed repo skills.

techniques.title: Route content operations through the owning abstraction
techniques.body: Document Service owns high-level content access; raw queries belong only in the database package. Content-type schemas generate tables, so ordinary changes do not need raw migrations.
techniques.quote: Always use this for reading/writing content — never raw DB queries unless you're working inside `@strapi/database` itself.

techniques.title: Separate edition toggles across testing layers
techniques.body: Frontend and end-to-end tests use different environment variables to enable Enterprise behavior. The guide lists both alongside Community Edition frontend commands, making the distinction explicit for verification.
techniques.quote:
- `IS_EE=true` — enables Enterprise features in frontend tests (`yarn test:front`)
- `RUN_EE=true` — enables Enterprise features in E2E tests

techniques.title: Identify stale generated test apps as misleading evidence
techniques.body: API integration test applications are generated automatically. The instructions require regeneration before reuse and explain that stale apps can produce failures unrelated to the current change.
techniques.quote: always regenerate with `yarn test:generate-app` rather than reusing a stale one (stale apps cause misleading failures).

techniques.title: Distinguish an absent optional tool from a broken one
techniques.body: A missing optional brain-start skill is a normal no-op for external contributors. If the installed tool fails to refresh, report and fix the failure.
techniques.quote: Only the absence of the optional skill is a clean no-op.

steal: Name real exceptions to sandbox-only editing rules.
Keep committed skills in one canonical location.
Route data operations through the abstraction that owns them.
Document distinct test toggles for product editions.
Regenerate fixtures before interpreting integration failures.
Distinguish absent optional integrations from failed installed ones.
